contributions.text: 3. What progress her Department has made on reforming the SEND system.
contributions.name: Nadia Whittome

contributions.who: The Minister for School Standards (Georgia Gould)
contributions.text: The Department is investing £4 billion over this year and the next two years to help children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities to receive support. We are training teachers, investing in new specialist places and mainstream schools, rolling out experts at hand and strengthening local partnerships. We are continuing to carefully consider responses to the consultation and engaging widely. We will publish our consultation response and bring forward legislation early in the new year.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: Under the Government’s plans to reform the SEND system, millions of pupils will be given individual support plans agreed between parents and schools, but, unlike education, health and care plans, those will not be subject to independent legal appeal. Campaigners and my constituents are worried that parents may be left with no legal route to challenge a school if a child is not getting the right support. Can the Minister reassure them that that will not be the case?
contributions.name: Nadia Whittome

contributions.text: Legal duties on schools to identify and support children’s needs are getting stronger. We are developing new national standards for the first time, with new duties on schools to develop individual support plans with families and young people and a stronger role for Ofsted in overseeing inclusion. We want to build a system based on partnership with families and young people at its heart. We have been working closely with families and young people, listening to their reflections on our plans, and we have heard clearly from families how important accountability is. That is why we are taking the time to ensure that we are getting the plans right. We will publish a full response to the consultation.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: I have been campaigning for a number of years for the Bilton Woodfield specialist school for autism and SEND to open. A phased approach means that many parents remain understandably concerned that their children have missed out on the process. Will the Minister agree to meet me to talk about more specialist SEND and autism school places and ensure that reforms focus on those, too?
contributions.name: Tom Gordon

contributions.text: I would be delighted to meet the hon. Member. We are investing £3.7 billion in creating new specialist places and see special schools as playing a really important role in the new system. I am happy to take forward that conversation.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: I call the Chair of the Education Committee.
contributions.name: Chair

contributions.text: The Education Committee has heard overwhelming evidence that one of the essential conditions for successful SEND reform will be the extent to which NHS services are accountable for playing their part in delivering the healthcare services that children with special educational needs and disabilities require to access education. We have been disappointed with the engagement from the Department of Health and Social Care on this issue so far. Will the Minister confirm what discussions she is having with her counterparts in that Department and whether the “education for all” Bill will include measures to ensure the accountability of NHS services in the SEND system?
contributions.name: Helen Hayes

contributions.text: I share my hon. Friend’s concern that too many young people are falling through the cracks between different services. It is critical that education, health and social care are working together. I reassure her that I am working really closely with my counterparts in the Department of Health and Social Care. That was a big issue that came from the consultation, and we are working closely together to bring forward proposals.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: Many parents and carers in my constituency are backing calls to end attendance fines for families whose children cannot attend school because of unmet SEND needs while they wait months—sometimes years—for assessment. What steps is the Minister taking to ensure that families already at breaking point are supported rather than penalised?
contributions.name: Manuela Perteghella

contributions.text: The hon. Member is right that we need to have a support-first approach to families; that is what our guidance sets out. We are putting in place a whole range of new support to wrap around families and schools—for example, the new experts-at-hand service is starting to be rolled out by councils around the country; and we are bringing forward work on family first partnerships to provide early help for families—and we are determined that that happens in practice in every part of the country.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould
